A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All 21 pages of v2 and 23 pages of v3, including appendices A–G, are readable, and the original figures, tables, and experimental content can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original intent/topic classification experiments, ASR evaluations, and supplementary analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original classification experiments, ASR evaluations, and supplementary analyses, including their numerical results.

M1.justification: The text-only, speech-only, and ASR-to-text cascaded procedures retain the same components and training approaches. Cascades trained on ASR transcriptions already appear in v2 Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same German/Bavarian intent tasks using MASSIVE and xSID, and Swiss German topic classification using SwissDial. The fuller xSID-audio release documented in v3 does not broaden the reported experiments beyond the retained evaluation subsets.

E2.justification: The evaluated text models, speech/ASR models, majority and random baselines, and supplementary cascade configurations are unchanged. Newly discussed OpusLM, pixel-based, and multimodal models are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported splits, label mappings, lowercasing, model sizes, training budgets, metrics, and manual ASR sampling procedure remain unchanged. v3 newly states that training and evaluation speakers do not overlap; it does not describe changing the splits.

E4.justification: The learning-rate sensitivity analysis, ASR-trained cascade comparisons, manual transcription evaluation, and ASR error examples are retained in Appendices D–F. The new dataset sentence examples illustrate existing coverage rather than introduce another analytical test.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds, means and standard deviations, and the same Pearson correlations and significance reporting. v3's additional duration summaries continue the mean-and-standard-deviation practice already used in v2 Appendix A.

E6.justification: For the 412-example subsets, reported German/Bavarian audio durations change from 2.98±1.03/3.06±1.01 seconds in v2 Appendix A.3 to 3.48±1.05/3.52±1.02 seconds in v3 Table 7. Full-release duration statistics are also added. The cause of these revisions is unstated; all matched classification and ASR result tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The retained empirical comparison calculations and evaluation criteria introduce no revised mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, three principal introductory findings, and conclusion retain the same claims about modality-dependent dialect transfer and ASR normalization. The dialectal audio-intent dataset contribution retains its scope; its release status changes under D1.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive model-scope limitations: tokenized speech, continuous pixel-based text representations, and aligned multimodal models are not covered. It also qualifies statements about dialectal pretraining exposure. Existing mechanism hypotheses and read-speech/single-speaker limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 promises future dataset, code, and prediction releases; v3 reports public releases and supplies concrete Zenodo and GitHub access information. It specifies xSID-audio licensing and usage restrictions, documents the full release of 300 development and 500 test recordings per variety, adds SwissDial resource information, and discloses the absence of speaker overlap. This substantially expands reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused references supporting speech-data motivation and model limitations, including Chrupała, Scharenborg et al., Rust et al., Duquenne et al., and Tian et al. MMS is now attributed to Pratap et al. The main related-work framing and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 expands the introductory explanation of standard-to-dialect transfer, clarifies the language varieties and dataset documentation, and makes localized wording and bibliographic edits. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 1, 2, and 7 for sentence examples, dataset coverage, and audio statistics. It expands the resource table, corrects the manual-evaluation caption to identify the Acc column, and relocates existing tables, including ASR examples onto a separate page. Figure 1 and existing result-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Concrete resource access information replaces promised releases, dataset summaries distinguish the full release from the evaluated subset, and new model limitations better qualify generalization. These improve reproducibility documentation and clarity while preserving the experimental evidence. The unexplained duration revisions leave a small reporting ambiguity, but the net quality gain is supported and limited.
